title: Integrated Pest & Disease Management (IPM)
summary: Combine cultural, biological, and physical controls before considering chemical interventions.
tips: Scout fields at least twice a week, checking leaf undersides and soil interfaces.
Install pheromone traps and yellow/blue sticky cards for early pest flight detection.
Conserve natural predators such as ladybird beetles, lacewings, and predatory spiders.
Use chemicals only as a last resort, following label dosages strictly and rotating modes of action.

title: Smart Irrigation & Moisture Control
summary: Foliage wetness is the number one driver of fungal and bacterial infections.
tips: Adopt drip irrigation or furrow irrigation instead of overhead sprinklers.
Water crops early in the morning so morning sun evaporates residual foliage moisture quickly.
Apply organic mulch (straw, dried leaves, dry husk) to reduce evaporation and prevent soil-borne spore backsplashes.
Maintain drainage channels to avoid standing water during heavy monsoon rains.

title: Soil Health & Nutrient Balancing
summary: Healthy plants with balanced cellular structure naturally resist pathogen penetration.
tips: Test your soil pH and nutrient profile every two seasons before major sowings.
Avoid excessive synthetic nitrogen, which creates tender, watery plant tissues vulnerable to blights and pests.
Incorporate organic compost, farmyard manure, and green manure crops (sunn hemp, dhaincha).
Ensure adequate potassium and silica to strengthen leaf cuticle thickness.

title: Clean Seed & Nursery Sanitation
summary: Over 60% of crop diseases enter farms via contaminated seed lots or seedling nurseries.
tips: Always source certified, disease-free seed batches from registered agricultural stations.
Perform seed priming and biological treatment using Trichoderma viride or Pseudomonas fluorescens.
Disinfect nursery trays, knives, and pruning shears regularly with 10% bleach solution or 70% alcohol.
Rogue out and destroy weak or stunted nursery seedlings before transplanting into main fields.

title: Safe Agricultural Chemical Handling
summary: Protect farmer health and environmental safety during any agricultural application.
tips: Always wear complete personal protective equipment (PPE): gloves, eye mask, and respirator.
Never mix two unauthorized pesticides together; follow label compatibility charts.
Do not spray against the direction of the wind or during hot midday hours.
Respect Pre-Harvest Intervals (PHI) strictly to prevent harmful residues in consumer foods.
Triple-rinse and puncture empty pesticide containers before authorized disposal.
